chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abu al-Husayn al-Nakha'i, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I was standing performing salat (prayer), while Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام was sitting before me and I did not know. Then 'Abbad al-Basri came to him, greeted him, and sat down. He said to him: O Abu al-Hasan, what do you say about a man who performed tamattu' and had no sacrificial offering? He said: He fasts the days that Allah, Exalted is He, has stated.

He said: So I turned my hearing toward them. 'Abbad said to him: Which days are they? He said: They are one day before al-Tarwiyah, the Day of al-Tarwiyah, and the Day of 'Arafah. He said: If he misses that, then what? He said: He fasts the morning of al-Hasbah and two days after that. He said: Will you not say as 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan said? He said: And what did he say? He said: He fasts the days of al-Tashriq. He said: Ja'far used to say: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ordered Bilal to proclaim: These are days of eating and drinking, so no one should fast.
He said: O Abu al-Hasan, indeed Allah, Exalted is He, said: “then a fast of three days during the hajj (pilgrimage) and seven when you return.”
He said: Ja'far used to say: The whole of Dhu al-Hijjah is among the months of hajj (pilgrimage).

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: the days after Eid al-Adha, described here as days of eating and drinking
key_terms.الْحَجِّ: the period and rites of hajj (pilgrimage)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: performed hajj al-tamattu', the pilgrimage mode combining 'umrah and hajj
key_terms.ذُو الْحِجَّةِ: the month in which the hajj rites take place
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: the sacrificial offering required in tamattu' hajj
key_terms.يَصُومُ: he fasts as a substitute act of worship when the offering is unavailable
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth of Dhu al-Hijjah, a designated day in the hajj rites
key_terms.يَوْمُ عَرَفَةَ: the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah, the day of standing at 'Arafat

ai.seo_question: Which days should a pilgrim fast if he performs tamattu' and cannot find the sacrificial offering?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for one performing hajj tamattu' who cannot find the sacrificial offering and must instead fast. It specifies which three days are to be fasted and rejects fasting during the days of al-Tashriq by citing a prophetic proclamation that they are days of eating and drinking. It also explains the Quranic phrase about fasting during hajj by affirming that the whole of Dhu al-Hijjah counts within the hajj period.
